themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints skyrocketed to 4 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,100% spike (z-score: 11.72)—suggesting rapid deterioration of dining structures, safety hazards, or encroachment issues as the season opens in Park Slope.
evidence: 4 outdoor dining complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3,100% increase)
Z-score of 11.72 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Spike timing aligns with spring/summer dining season reopening (early April 2026)
reporting_angles: Which restaurants have unsafe or code-violating outdoor structures? Interview DOT and community residents.
Are sidewalk sheds and dining enclosures blocking pedestrian access or creating ADA compliance issues?

themes_detail.label: Street Signage Structural Failure
themes_detail.summary: Dangling street signs spiked to 5 complaints 2 weeks ago versus 0.5 weekly average (900% increase, z-score: 6.36), and damaged signs hit 5 complaints last week versus 1.0 average (400% increase, z-score: 4.0)—indicating widespread infrastructure deterioration requiring urgent DOT repair.
evidence: Dangling signs: 5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (900% spike, z-score: 6.36)
Damaged signs: 5 complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly baseline (400% spike, z-score: 4.0)
Two simultaneous spikes in street sign complaints within 1-week window suggest systemic issue
reporting_angles: Walk Park Slope and Carroll Gardens to document which streets have dangerous hanging or damaged signs; safety liability.
Interview DOT about maintenance backlog and timeline for repairs—is this weather-related or chronic understaffing?

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees & Branches Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints jumped to 7 this week versus 1.5 weekly average 2 weeks ago (367% increase, z-score: 5.5), and abandoned bikes spiked to 8 complaints (300% increase, z-score: 4.0)—suggesting Parks Department neglect of public green space maintenance.
evidence: Overgrown tree/branches: 7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.5 weekly baseline (367% spike, z-score: 5.5)
Abandoned bikes: 8 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.0 weekly baseline (300% spike, z-score: 4.0)
Both spikes indicate parks and public space neglect entering spring growing season
Community Board budget requests repeatedly ask for 'reconstruct or upgrade park amenities' (ongoing, unsolved issue)
reporting_angles: Survey Prospect Park, Carroll Park, and other district parks for overgrown branches blocking sidewalks/sight lines; talk to residents about safety concerns.
Interview Parks Department about 2026 tree maintenance and removal budget—is this symptomatic of resource shortfall?

themes_detail.label: Building Code & Use Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Building/use complaints surged to 9 this week versus 1.8 weekly average 3 weeks ago (414% increase, z-score: 3.91), coinciding with 74 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (33 new buildings, 30 alterations)—suggesting code enforcement gaps amid active development.
evidence: Building/use complaints: 9 reports 3 weeks ago vs. 1.8 weekly baseline (414% spike, z-score: 3.91)
74 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (33 new buildings + 30 alterations suggest heavy construction activity)
Active ULURP applications (46 Nelson Street rezoning, GSD certifications) indicate neighborhood-scale development pressure
reporting_angles: Which specific buildings are generating the most complaints? Cross-reference 311 with DOB permits to identify problem projects.
Are contractors operating outside permitted hours or violating safety protocols? Interview neighbors and DOB enforcement.

themes_detail.label: Animal Safety Concern in Parks
themes_detail.summary: Animal-in-park complaints jumped to 4 reports 3 weeks ago versus 0.6 weekly average (540% increase, z-score: 6.97)—potentially indicating loose or aggressive animals, wildlife intrusion, or inadequate park monitoring.
evidence: Animal-in-park complaints: 4 reports 3 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (540% spike, z-score: 6.97)
Community Board budget requests mention 'enhance park safety through more security staff' (recurring, unmet need)
Timing aligns with spring season when animals become more active in urban parks
reporting_angles: What animals have been reported? Interview Parks enforcement and residents to document specific incidents.
Are park patrols insufficient to monitor and respond to animal safety issues? Link to CB budget requests for security staffing.
